title: Foreign Acquisitions and Takeovers Fees Imposition Amendment (Fee Streamlining and Other Measures) Bill 2017
short_title: Foreign Acquisitions and Takeovers Fees Imposition Amendment (Fee Streamlining and Other Measures) Bill 2017

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would restructure foreign investment application fees by introducing fewer commercial fee tiers and flat charges, while increasing certain residential property fees.
Residential purchase fees would rise by 10 per cent for acquisitions worth $10 million or less, including relevant purchases covered by exemption certificates.
The new fee framework would apply from 1 July 2017, with indexation paused for affected fees during 2017-18 and resuming in 2018-19.
changes: Commercial land and business acquisition fees would use three value bands.
Applications for land exemption certificates under section 58 would attract a single $35,000 fee.
Variations of non-residential commercial exemption certificates would carry a flat $10,100 charge.
summary.affected: Foreign investors, property developers and businesses seeking foreign investment approval would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Luke Howarth
speeches.brief: The coalition government argued the Foreign Acquisitions and Takeovers Fees Imposition Amendment Bill 2017 streamlines foreign investment fees, reduces red tape, and introduces a standard fee based on acquisition value. The speech defended foreign investment regulation by citing examples like the Kidman cattle station sale and Darwin port lease, and highlighted measures such as a vacancy charge on foreign-owned residential properties to boost rental stock.

speeches.speaker: Keith Pitt
speeches.brief: The bill amends the Foreign Acquisitions and Takeovers Fees Imposition Amendment Bill 2017 to streamline foreign investment fees, reduce complexity, and introduce a 10 per cent fee increase for residential property applications to fund the Critical Infrastructure Centre.
